brief: UBS sales desk commentary spanning macro, Nvidia, FX and cross-asset one-liners. NY Fed's Williams shifted from no 2027 hikes needed to signaling gradual continued increases, and UBS reads this as evidence he, not Waller, is now Chair Warsh's top lieutenant. Nvidia ousted CEO Jensen Huang, with CFO Colette Kress named interim. Huang will testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Analyst Timothy Arcuri argues Huang's absence will pause Nvidia's deal-making with neo-clouds and ecosystem partners, and that tighter US restrictions could still hit NVDA and AMD shipments to China and to Singapore and Malaysia. Separately, OpenAI is backing Congress bills to curb China's AI-chip access, and Lutnick faces ouster pressure over Nvidia China-export oversight. Japan's Katayama warned of FX action after USDJPY breached 160. The desk's own flow view says the move is dollar-led, not yen-led, so intervention would likely fail given unchanged rate differentials. Trump claimed Iran victory and wants to disengage even as three carrier groups with 60,000 personnel arrive in the Gulf and the IAEA says it has lost track of Iran's uranium. Also covers Microsoft's outage, Australia CPI, memory-chip calls, an AUD curve trade and Brazil.
